description:
Redwood Inference is running a cross-functional Finance/Legal/RevOps + Product + Engineering initiative to (1) validate and harden billing meters (Hosted API tokens/requests, embeddings batch accounting, retries/idempotency behavior, cache-hit attribution, Dedicated GPU-seconds) and (2) analyze recent/prior pricing & packaging experiments to publish clear internal guidance for go-to-market and contracting. The project exists because Redwood’s usage-based business model depends on high-integrity telemetry: small metering bugs (double-counting retries, missing dimensions, inconsistent token counting across OpenAI-compatible endpoints, late-arriving events) can create invoice disputes, revenue recognition risk, and distorted experiment conclusions.

Goals & deliverables:
- Meter sanity checks: a formal meter spec, a reconciliation playbook (ledger vs usage events vs customer-facing usage API), automated daily/weekly drift checks, and dashboards/alerts for data-quality SLOs.
- Meter fixes & hardening: engineering changes to prevent double-counting, improve idempotency, align token counting across endpoints, add integration tests and perf-canary regression scenarios, and add a “shadow billing compare” mode before changes affect invoices.
- Experiment analysis: define cohorts/metrics/stop criteria, produce readouts (conversion, retention, ARPU, gross margin), and document recommendations on packaging variants, free tier/overage, and discount/credit guardrails.
- Publish guidance: updated Confluence pages for pricing/packaging, RevRec/billing procedures, and Sales Enablement FAQs; plus legal language guidance for usage definitions in MSAs/order forms.

Stakeholders:
- Finance/RevRec: Laura Bennett (CFO), Rishi Malhotra (FP&A), Emily Stone (Accounting).
- Legal: Michael Grant (GC), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel).
- Product/RevOps: Evelyn Hart (CPO), Nikhil Sharma (Dir PM Hosted API), Chris Osei (Product Ops), Jordan Blake (CRO).
- Engineering: Logan Wright (EM Telemetry), Nadia Rahman (Staff Telemetry), Ethan Park (EM Platform Control Plane), Cole Summers (Billing Hooks).

Scope & timeline (typical 6–8 week push):
1) Week 1–2: meter audit + discrepancy sampling; agree on definitions and “source of truth” tables.
2) Week 2–4: implement fixes, add tests, add exports/dashboards, run shadow-billing comparisons.
3) Week 4–6: experiment readouts, margin model updates, pricing guidance draft.
4) Week 6–8: exec sign-off, sales enablement rollout, legal language updates, and operational runbooks/alerts turned on.

Constraints:
- Customer-sensitive billing data and legal terms (restricted sharing).
- Avoid retroactive invoice changes without Finance/Legal approval; prefer forward fixes with audit trails.
- Ensure experiment conclusions aren’t biased by meter changes (explicit “pre/post meter fix” segmentation).
